title: feat: the next action and the owner's decisions are kept as data
headline: A project's next action, what waits on the owner, the carry-overs and the kit version now live once, in _State.json, and the owner's rulings in _Decisions.jsonl; the Resume Point and the dashboard lines are generated from them, and a check fails the moment they drift.
alignment: v1.34.0 is the first v2.0 step after the sweep shape: T4, state as data. On 1.33.1 four tracking files stated the next action by hand and three were two releases stale; now one file does, and the views cannot drift unseen.

items.text: The state script keeps the next action, what blocks on the owner, what only waits, the carry-overs, the phase and the kit version in _State.json, and writes the Resume Point and the dashboard lines from them.
items.before: Stated by hand in four files
items.after: Kept once; the views are generated

items.text: What blocks on the owner and what only waits for the owner's eyes are two lists, so a note for the owner no longer stops the work.

The owner's rulings are kept in _Decisions.jsonl with an id, the date, the owner's exact words and the reason; the words must be found in the owner's own messages or pop-up answers, or are marked as not checked. Rows are only ever added.
items.before: Spread over plans and memory, no ids

items.text: state.mjs check fails when a view differs from the data, a label sits outside its block, the installed kit is newer than the data says, a committed decision changed, or a D-n pointer has no record; the use check and status report it.
An existing project moves its filled-in Resume Point into the data once with state.mjs init, which refuses anything it cannot move whole and changes nothing then.
The closeout sets the state with state.mjs commands instead of hand edits, and its hand-back ends with the next item, so the coordinator can open the next thread at once.
state.mjs never writes through a linked tracking file, leaves no temporary file behind, refuses a planted item id, and the use check runs the kit's own copy of it, never the project's.

verification: Each behaviour has a test that fails on the code before it (8 of the new state tests failed on the first build's script; all failed before it existed).
A trial on a copy of the workbench's 1.33.1 tracking files: init moved the stale Resume Point into the data and check passed; a closeout now has 3 hand edits, against 10 to 15.
Recall: median 14 of 14 over 5 runs against the 1.33.1 baseline of 14, control 0, scored blind (gate line k134-final).

decisions.decision: State and decisions first; the list and the roadmap as data next
decisions.why: The owner picked this slice by pop-up: it fixes the drift that was proven, with one small review; the list and the roadmap follow in 1.35.0.

decisions.decision: A hand edit inside a block is refused, not overwritten
decisions.why: The sweep found render wiped a carry-over typed into the block; render now keeps a hash of what it wrote and writes over a changed block only when told to, after the change is in the data.

decisions.decision: The owner's words must be found where he said them
decisions.why: The kit's approach rests on the owner's word being his own; a decision row points to the turn its words came from and is checked again there.
